title: Interac Debit Online After Interac Online
description: Interac Online has been retired. How Interac Debit now works online through Apple Pay and Google Pay, what Shopify, WooCommerce and Square document, and a test.
h1: Interac Debit online: what replaced Interac Online
name: Interac Debit online
lead: Interac Online, the old redirect-to-your-bank checkout, is gone. Canadians can still pay online with Interac Debit, but now it runs inside Apple Pay and Google Pay, through whichever payment processor your store uses. Whether your checkout takes it depends on that processor, and the platforms say little about it.
factsHeading: Interac Debit online at a glance

facts.label: Interac Online
facts.value: No longer available as of Oct 31, 2024

facts.label: How it works now
facts.value: Buyer chooses Apple Pay or Google Pay at checkout, selects Interac Debit, then authenticates

facts.label: Buyer needs
facts.value: A Canadian bank account at a participating institution, a debit card, and Apple Pay or Google Pay on a device

facts.label: Merchant needs
facts.value: An acquirer; Interac lists Moneris, Square, Stripe, Adyen, Global Payments and others, without saying which support online

facts.label: Merchant fees
facts.value: Set by your acquirer and include Interac's fees

facts.label: Shopify in person
facts.value: Interac debit by tap or chip and PIN on Shopify POS with the Tap & Chip reader

facts.label: Shopify online
facts.value: Shopify Payments in Canada takes credit and debit cards and accelerated checkouts; Interac is not named

facts.label: Square
facts.value: Accepts Interac debit cards and supports Apple Pay, Google Pay and Samsung Pay

body: For years, Interac Online sent shoppers from a store's checkout to their bank's website to approve a payment. Interac's own notice says it is no longer available as of Oct 31, 2024. If an old plugin, payment page or FAQ on your site still offers it, take it down; the option will fail at checkout.

What replaced it for most shoppers is Interac Debit inside a digital wallet. A customer adds their debit card to Apple Pay or Google Pay, and at a participating merchant chooses the wallet at checkout, picks Interac Debit, and approves with a fingerprint, face or passcode. Interac lists the participating banks and credit unions, and the big Canadian banks are on that list.

You do not sign up with Interac directly. Your acquirer, the payment processor behind your checkout, carries Interac Debit for you and sets the fee, which includes Interac's charges. Interac's business page lists acquirers including Moneris, Square, Stripe, Adyen and Global Payments, but it does not say which of them support online Interac Debit as opposed to in-store terminals.

Interac says merchants get funds quickly with no chargebacks on Interac Debit. That is a real difference from credit cards, so it is worth asking your processor whether wallet payments made with an Interac card are processed as Interac or as another network.

Shopify documents Interac clearly for in-person sales: Shopify POS takes Interac debit by tap or chip and PIN on its Tap & Chip reader. For the online store, Shopify Payments in Canada says it takes credit and debit cards and accelerated checkouts, but its help pages do not name Interac Debit online. Shopify's wallet pages show how to turn on Apple Pay and Google Pay; whether an Interac card in the wallet goes through as Interac is not something Shopify's pages confirm.

WooCommerce's payment extensions are in the same position. WooPayments and the Stripe extension both offer Apple Pay and Google Pay, and Stripe appears on Interac's acquirer list, but we found no WooCommerce page that names Interac Debit for online orders.

Square accepts Interac debit cards and supports Apple Pay, Google Pay and Samsung Pay, and it is on Interac's acquirer list. Its Canadian help page does not spell out how an Interac card in a wallet is handled on Square Online. If this matters to your margins, ask Square support in writing.

sections.h2: Test it with a real card
body: The only reliable check is a real purchase. Add an Interac debit card from a participating bank to Apple Pay or Google Pay, buy a low-priced item from your own store, and look at the transaction in your payment dashboard. It will show the card network and the fee charged. Then refund it and confirm the refund lands back on the debit card.

steps.name: Remove Interac Online
steps.text: Delete any old Interac Online gateway, button or mention from your checkout and help pages.

steps.name: Turn on wallets
steps.text: Enable Apple Pay and Google Pay in your store's payment settings.

steps.name: Ask your processor
steps.text: Ask whether Interac debit cards in wallets are processed as Interac for your account, and at what fee.

steps.name: Make a test purchase
steps.text: Pay with an Interac card in a wallet, check the network and fee in your dashboard, then refund it.

checklist: No page on your site still mentions Interac Online
Apple Pay and Google Pay show at checkout on a phone
A test payment with an Interac card in a wallet completes
You know the fee your processor charges for it

faqs.q: Can customers still pay online with a Canadian debit card?
faqs.a: Yes, through Apple Pay or Google Pay with Interac Debit at participating banks, if your processor supports it.

faqs.q: Do I need a contract with Interac?
faqs.a: No. Interac Debit comes through your acquirer, which also sets the fee.

faqs.q: Is Interac e-Transfer the same thing?
faqs.a: No. An e-Transfer is a bank-to-bank transfer you confirm by hand. Interac Debit online is a wallet payment approved at checkout.
